claims.text: Earlier, in FOI-1730-1819, TfL stated it would undertake rail grinding between Bethnal Green and Mile End in February 2019 to improve the wheel-rail interface after measurements confirmed elevated rail roughness levels between 720 and 880m.

citations.quote: We will undertake rail grinding at this location in February 2019, with the intention to improve the wheel-rail interface.

citations.quote: Readings are carried out on a bi-monthly period.

claims.text: Under The Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 cited by TfL for worker occupational health, the lower exposure action value is a daily personal noise exposure level (LEPd) of 80 dB(A), the upper exposure action value is 85 dB(A), and the exposure limit value is 87 dB(A).

citations.quote: the 'lower exposure action value', corresponding to a daily personal noise exposure level of 80 dB(A);
the 'upper exposure action value', corresponding to a daily personal noise exposure level of 85 dB(A);
and the 'exposure limit value', corresponding to a daily personal noise exposure level of 87 dB(A).

claims.text: In our uncalibrated relative phone-audio recordings in the passenger saloon, mean levels were -18.66 dBFS(A) on eastbound LST-BTH (n=6) and -19.42 dBFS(A) on eastbound BTH-MLE (n=6), and -18.8 dBFS(A) on westbound BTH-LST (n=5) and -19.07 dBFS(A) on westbound MLE-BTH (n=5).

Across n=11 paired trips in our uncalibrated relative phone-audio measurements, the mean within-trip difference between LST-BTH and BTH-MLE was 0.54 dB (sd 0.36 dB, range -0.13 to 1.21 dB), resulting in a pre-registered NO-GO verdict because the contrast is under 1 dB and inside limiter compression and run-to-run variation.

In our uncalibrated relative phone-audio data, eastbound LST-BTH (-18.66 dBFS(A)) was 4.01 dB higher than the sub-surface Hammersmith & City and Circle line section between Liverpool Street and Aldgate East (-22.67 dBFS(A)) and 4.85 dB higher than Central line Holborn to Chancery Lane (-23.51 dBFS(A)).

Separate indicative measurements using the NIOSH sound level meter app on an iPhone in the passenger saloon over one whole trip per direction (including platform and dwell time) recorded 91.9 dB(A) LAeq eastbound from Liverpool Street to Mile End (n=1) and 87.3 dB(A) LAeq westbound from Mile End to Liverpool Street (n=1), though the app is validated only up to about 85 dB(A) so readings above 85 dB(A) may read low and are not like-for-like with TfL's per-section in-cab figures.

A secondary press report in Brixton Buzz (attributing information to JRPass) cites 92.8 decibels for Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green, but this is not a primary TfL disclosure in the corpus and neither its measurement location (cab vs saloon) nor its underlying TfL source is established.

claims.text: The public record in the corpus does not establish which track direction (eastbound, westbound, or both) was ground between December 2021 and May 2022 on LST-BTH and BTH-MLE, whether either section has been ground again since May 2022, or whether the planned eastbound LST-BTH deep Tube reconditioning was completed.

At Mayor's Question Time on 16 July 2026 (2026/2156), Elly Baker AM reported that TfL's Government Relations team had turned down the majority of her requests for Tube noise data and noted that rail grinding is only planned eight weeks in advance, prompting the Mayor to promise far more detailed information on rail grinding and track renewal programmes.

citations.quote: just an email from TfL's Government Relations turning down the majority of the requests for data.
We cannot do that because it is only planned eight weeks in advance

I will make sure it provides, in addition, information on what in real-time rail grinding activity is taking place over the next six months, the track renewal programmes, alternative noise reduction measures that are being considered or in delivery.

asks.request: Please provide the complete log of all rail grinding carried out on the Central line between Liverpool Street and Bethnal Green and between Bethnal Green and Mile End from December 2021 to the present, specifying for each intervention the exact dates, direction (eastbound or westbound), chainage/metres ground, and whether the eight-week rolling programme currently schedules further grinding on either section.
asks.why: Closes the gap on which direction was ground in Dec 2021-May 2022 and whether repeat grinding has been carried out at the 6-12 month interval TfL says is needed to maintain effectiveness (C1, C3, C14, C15).

asks.request: Please confirm whether the Deep Tube Reconditioning (Pandrol Vanguard conversion to Delkor) planned for 2023/24 on Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green Eastbound was completed, provide the completion date and chainage covered, and state whether Pandrol Vanguard fastenings remain in place on either direction of LST-BTH or BTH-MLE.
asks.why: Clarifies whether the planned track reconditioning on LST-BTH eastbound actually took place before or after TfL's June 2024 cab measurements (C4, C5, C14).

asks.request: Please provide all bi-monthly in-cab LAeq noise measurements and any passenger saloon noise or rail roughness (corrugation) measurements recorded for the Central line sections Liverpool Street-Bethnal Green and Bethnal Green-Mile End (both directions) from 2021 to the present, and clarify whether TfL holds any dataset containing a 92.8 dB figure for Liverpool Street-Bethnal Green.
asks.why: Establishes the full bi-monthly time series of in-cab noise levels before and after grinding, provides any passenger saloon data to compare with cab readings, and resolves the provenance of the secondary 92.8 dB press figure (C5, C7, C12, C13).
